fresh_terms.name: ~aNonce
fresh_terms.purpose: ANonce generated freshly by Alex/A at the start of a run

fresh_terms.name: ~bNonce
fresh_terms.purpose: BNonce generated freshly by Blake/B after receiving Alex's nonce

messages.label: M1
messages.meaning: Alex/A sends ANonce in clear to Blake/B.

messages.label: M2
messages.meaning: Blake/B sends BNonce in clear to Alex/A after receiving an ANonce value.

messages.label: M3
messages.meaning: After installing SK = kdf(ANonce,BNonce), Alex/A sends the fixed string ACK in clear to Blake/B.

checks: Bind received network term as ANonce_from_M1; no cryptographic verification or authentication check is described.
Bind received network term as BNonce_from_M2; no cryptographic verification or authentication check is described.
Check received network term equals the fixed string 'ACK'; ACK carries no nonce, identity, MAC, signature, or session-key binding.

checks.condition: Bind the received M1 payload as ANonce_from_M1; no tag, encryption, signature, freshness test, or source authentication is present.
Bind the received M2 payload as BNonce_from_M2; no tag, encryption, signature, freshness test, or source authentication is present.
Check that the received M3 payload is exactly the literal string 'ACK'.

events.name: IN_M2
events.when: A receives a network value in the BNonce position

events.name: A_Install

events.name: OUT_M3

events.when: A switches to DONE after sending ACK

events.name: IN_M3
events.when: B receives and accepts the fixed ACK literal

events.name: B_Install
events.when: B derives and installs sk = kdf(aNonce,bNonce) after receiving ACK

events.name: B_Secret
events.when: B has installed the session key whose secrecy is claimed by sk_secret_b

events.name: B_Done
events.when: B switches to DONE after installing the session key

claims.intent: There exists an honest execution in which A and B both complete the described protocol and reach DONE after installing the same kdf-derived session key.
claims.witness: Honest delivery trace: A sends ~aNonce; B receives ~aNonce and sends ~bNonce; A receives ~bNonce, installs kdf(~aNonce,~bNonce), sends 'ACK', and reaches DONE; B receives 'ACK', installs kdf(~aNonce,~bNonce), and reaches DONE.

claims.intent: The session key installed by A at A_Secret should remain secret from the adversary; the supplied expected result says this all-traces secrecy property is falsified.
claims.witness: In an honest run, M1 exposes ~aNonce and M2 exposes ~bNonce on the Dolev-Yao network. Since kdf/2 is public, the adversary can compute kdf(~aNonce,~bNonce), matching A's installed key when A receives the honest BNonce.

claims.intent: The session key installed by B at B_Secret should remain secret from the adversary; the supplied expected result says this all-traces secrecy property is falsified.
claims.witness: In an honest run, M1 exposes ~aNonce and M2 exposes ~bNonce on the Dolev-Yao network. Since kdf/2 is public, the adversary can compute kdf(~aNonce,~bNonce), matching B's installed key when B received the honest ANonce.

compromise.policy: No explicit Reveal, corruption, or long-term key compromise behavior is mentioned. The only adversarial exposure described is the standard Dolev-Yao network, under which plaintext M1, M2, and M3 are observable and replayable.

The session-key installation and DONE states are represented by A_Install/B_Install and A_Done/B_Done events.
The text says the established key can later be used to encrypt messages, but no post-establishment encrypted application traffic is specified; no such traffic is modeled.
Network send and receive are represented symbolically by messages and OUT/IN events under a Dolev-Yao adversarial network.
The secrecy proof interface uses A_Secret and B_Secret events at the points where the corresponding role installs SK; the source goals provide lemma names but no explicit action-fact vocabulary.
modeling_assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.
ANonce and BNonce are fresh nonces generated by A and B respectively.
Messages M1, M2, and M3 are unencrypted plaintext because the description gives only bare nonces and the literal ACK with no cryptographic wrapper.
B's state after M1 stores the received network value as ANonce_from_M1 and its generated ~bNonce until ACK is received.
A's state after M1 stores its generated ~aNonce until a BNonce-position network value is received.
No long-term keys are modeled because none are described.
The fixed ACK is not bound to either nonce, identity, or session key.

resolved_open_questions.question: Do A and B denote Alex and Blake?
resolved_open_questions.resolution: Yes. The description names Alex and Blake and immediately gives message notation A -> B and B -> A, so A is treated as Alex and B as Blake.
resolved_open_questions.evidence: Alex computes a nonce and sends it to Blake. (A -> B: ANonce)

semantic_constraints.policy: Do not add encryption, signatures, MACs, tags, certificates, identities inside messages, or nonce echoes not present in the source protocol.
M1 must precede B's generation and sending of M2 in an honest responder run.
A derives and installs SK_A = kdf(~aNonce,BNonce_from_M2) only after receiving a value in the M2/BNonce position.
A sends the literal 'ACK' only after installing SK_A.
B derives and installs SK_B = kdf(ANonce_from_M1,~bNonce) only after receiving and accepting a value equal to the literal 'ACK'.
For an untampered honest trace, B receives ANonce_from_M1 = ~aNonce and A receives BNonce_from_M2 = ~bNonce, so SK_A = SK_B = kdf(~aNonce,~bNonce).
For adversarial traces, received nonce-position values may be attacker-chosen or replayed; the protocol description contains no checks guaranteeing agreement between SK_A and SK_B.
The literal ACK can be injected or replayed by the adversary because it is public and unauthenticated.
